Statistical validation of llmsa

Source: vignettes/validation.Rmd
validation.Rmd

Variance components and gauge R&R (numeric)

These calculations compare the numeric random-effects model with independent ANOVA calculations, published estimates, certified NIST quantities and live package oracles. Every observed value is recomputed by the currently loaded llmsa namespace. No fitted estimates or oracle results are stored as inputs. The reference calculations are implemented in the installed validation/numeric/reference_checks.R script.

The reference authority is reference/anchors/: ANK-10 contains the AIAG example, ANK-13 the published Penicillin estimates, ANK-14 the NIST certified quantities, ANK-16 the GRR conventions, and ANK-TOL the comparison tolerances. Variance-component tolerances are fractions of the reference total variance; derived ratios use relative tolerances. Printed standard deviations are compared on the variance scale where the anchor requires it. The tables show the resulting absolute bounds.

This run uses the public context. A nonempty REPO_ROOT selects complete local validation: original anchors, the protected AIAG sheet and the frozen NIST originals. Missing inputs or mismatching SHA-256 hashes stop the calculation. Without REPO_ROOT, the public package build uses whole, byte-identical anchor copies and free NIST tables. Their provenance is recorded in validation/numeric/SOURCES.json. In that context, AIAG rows explicitly say not rerun: protected data required and never claim a successful rerun. Neither context displays the protected AIAG measurements.

The balanced synthetic studies use the specification’s four crossed designs with seed one, with and without block effects and pairwise interactions. The independent ANOVA calculation solves the expected-mean-square equations; negative moment estimates are outside that comparison. At a variance boundary, the numeric default fit re-estimates the remaining components by restricted REML. The AIAG comparison pools the interaction as in the handbook; that row is marked as not separately estimated. The model with interaction is reported separately. On the unbalanced ic50_demo data, VCA::remlVCA is a criterion, while VCA::anovaVCA is a reported comparison. SixSigma::ss.rr uses its default interaction pooling; study variation comes from its unrounded standard deviations.

NIST precision report

Item denotes the treatment and replicate denotes the observation within the treatment. The certified within mean square is the residual variance; the item reference is the between-minus-within mean-square difference divided by the number of replicates. NIST labels AtmWtAg as Average difficulty; the project nevertheless applies the stricter relative tolerance 10^{-8} to it, as to the lower-difficulty datasets.

Log relative error (LRE) is the negative base-ten logarithm of the absolute relative error. Exact agreement gives Inf. For SmLs04 through SmLs06, the required LRE is at least the corresponding stats::aov LRE minus 1. The higher-difficulty SmLs07 through SmLs09 are reports, with no pass threshold. Low LRE values expose precision loss, including loss in the original-scale lme4 model despite conditioning the variance-ratio calculation. NA denotes a failed fit whose reason is reported below; rounded input values are never repaired.

Reproduction and interpretation

Run Rscript data-raw/make_validation_numeric.R from the repository to reproduce the public inputs offline. The script checks original hashes before writing; --out <package-root> reproduces the files in a separate directory. The local NIST collection belongs in the sibling quellen/daten/ directory, and the protected AIAG sheet at the path recorded in ANK-10. The installed validation/numeric/README.md explains both build contexts and their checks.

The default numeric fit uses a closed EMS solution for eligible balanced designs and an analytic REML completion otherwise. Supplying any lme4 argument through ... selects the direct lme4 path; the ANOVA reference check uses the optimizer declared by ANK-TOL. The final model retains the original response scale, observation order and factor labels. Its components come from VarCorr(). Bootstrap refits use ordinary lme4 optimization with the stored refit control; the initial analytic completion is not repeated per replicate.

Zero total variance makes percentages, ICC and ndc undefined (NA), with verdict undetermined. Zero gauge variance with positive item variance gives infinite ndc; zero item variance with positive gauge variance gives the lower bound from ANK-16. Constant numeric responses and a degenerate residual variance produce named errors. These finite reference checks establish neither bootstrap coverage nor the later ordinal and binary simulation results.

Ordinal and binary outcomes (latent scale)

Ordinal msa_fit() uses cumulative link mixed models and binary msa_fit() uses binomial mixed models. Variance components, gauge R&R and ICC_items refer to the latent scale. ANK-28 fixes the residual variance to one for the probit link and to pi^2 / 3 for the logit link. In both cases, ICC_items is the item variance divided by the sum of all variance components, including that residual. Gauge R&R includes every component except the item variance.

All reference values below are read from ANK-21, ANK-25 and ANK-28, with tolerances from ANK-TOL. The public context verifies whole anchor copies and their SHA-256 manifest under validation/latent/. When REPO_ROOT is set, original anchors are also checked and used; an invalid root or missing input is an error. There is no network access.

Wine: ordinal components and a separate installation check

The wine comparison maps bottle to item, judge to prompt, with one model and one replicate. Each link is fitted again with ordinal::clmm and msa_fit(). The absolute comparison bound is ANK-TOL.engine_ordinal times the direct fit’s total latent variance. The tutorial’s clmm2 model includes temperature and contact fixed effects, so its ANK-21 estimates form a separate installation check, using both Laplace approximation and quadrature.

BeetlesMale: binary repeatability and a separate installation check

Population is the item, with one prompt, one model and replicates numbered within Population. The latent logit ICC_items is compared with live rptR::rptBinary(expect = "liability"), performance::icc() on both the direct glmer model and the returned model, and the independent calculation variance(Population) / (variance(Population) + pi^2 / 3) using ANK-28. These comparisons use ANK-TOL.rptr.live_tol.

The published ANK-25 values use rptR’s default expect = "meanobs" and a different scale convention. Both the link and original scale values are reproduced separately with ANK-TOL.rptr.vignette_tol. They are installation checks, not reference values for ICC_items.

Simulation recovery and two-level factors

The following tables read the installed studies’ <study>_results.csv if it exists, otherwise <study>_check_results.csv. An invalid existing full result file stops the build. The displayed n_sim comes from each file. Knitting does not rerun these class B simulations. Bias, relative bias, empirical standard error (EmpSE) and root mean squared error (RMSE) each have a Monte Carlo standard error (MCSE); the tables retain significant digits for small estimates. n_finite and n_failed count the usable and missing estimates separately. Finite estimates with non-convergence or singularity are retained, with the diagnoses recorded in the replicate and session files.

Short runs check reproducibility and file structure. They do not establish quantitative recovery or bias findings. Full runs require at least 1000 repetitions per scenario, according to ANK-06, and are performed separately by the operator after acceptance. The installed validation/sim/README.md gives executable full-run and scenario-merging instructions, the ADEMP design, MCSE formulas and failure handling. The random stream for each scenario and repetition is independent of the requested run length and worker count.

For ordinal fits, a prompt, model or block with exactly two levels enters as a fixed effect. Its component is the squared fitted difference divided by two, beta-hat^2 / 2, marked in attr(fit$vc, "derived") and in msa_grr(). This range method does not subtract the AIAG correction EV^2 / (n * r). Its bias is positive: E[beta-hat^2 / 2] = sigma^2 + Var(beta-hat) / 2. Every such fit warns, and printing names each derived component with range method, see ?msa_fit. The two_level study redraws both model effects in every repetition and reports derived_share, the fraction of repetitions with a derived model component. The full-run tables below report its measured bias and MCSE in each scenario. A bias that does not exceed the reporting threshold does not establish general unbiasedness. Fewer than three ordinal items are rejected.

Component findings use ANK-TOL.bias_report: the absolute relative bias must exceed both 0.1 and 3 times its MCSE. The two-level model bias is always reported; its direction is resolved only beyond 3 MCSE. These are reporting rules, not acceptance criteria for the estimates. Full-run findings are computed from the read tables, never selected by scenario name.

Ordinal convergence sensitivity

The main summaries above retain finite estimates even when a fit did not converge. The following separate analysis compares all finite estimates with only those whose recorded converged flag is true. Singular fits are retained in both eligible groups. Each n comes from the replicate rows used by that group, independently of the result table’s n_sim. Non-convergence, singularity and missing flags are counted separately per actual outer repetition.

Bias MCSE is EmpSE divided by the square root of n; relative bias and its MCSE divide by the truth and its absolute value, respectively. EmpSE MCSE uses the ADEMP approximation in the formula collection, section 9. Selecting on convergence can itself introduce selection bias: this comparison is a descriptive sensitivity analysis, not a replacement estimator or a reason to discard inconvenient estimates from the main study.

Bootstrap intervals: coverage by scenario

This section reads boot_coverage_results.csv (full run), with n_sim = 1000 repetitions per scenario. The installed boot_coverage_results.csv takes precedence over boot_coverage_check_results.csv. An invalid existing full result stops the build. This section reads the existing bootstrap results without rerunning the class B simulations or downloading inputs.

The study evaluates the existing 95% percentile intervals from msa_boot() for gauge R&R study variation and contribution, ndc and item ICC. Every outer repetition generates a new crossed study and uses the package’s default number of parametric bootstrap refits. Numeric scenarios include all three pairwise interactions; the binary logit scenario uses item, prompt and model effects. The installed validation/sim/README.md specifies the designs, seeds, Monte Carlo standard errors (MCSE), diagnostics and reproduction commands.

Coverage is the fraction of finite closed intervals containing the true value; width is their mean width. Their n_finite and n_failed count available and unavailable outer repetitions. For bootstrap diagnostics, the unit of analysis is also the outer repetition: each contributes its fraction of singular or failed refits, and MCSE is the standard error of the mean of those fractions. Singular refits with finite statistics remain in the intervals. Only non-finite values are omitted, separately for each statistic. The diagnostics count a replicate with any non-finite statistic as failed and do not also count it as singular.

Short runs establish reproducibility and file structure. They do not establish nominal coverage. Full runs require at least 1000 repetitions per scenario (ANK-06) and follow code acceptance. Undercoverage or overcoverage in those runs is a finding to report, with MCSE, rather than a reason to alter intervals. The reporting threshold is ANK-TOL.mc_factor.report, or 3 MCSE from the nominal level. A zero MCSE does not hide a deviation from nominal. The continuous GRR and ICC statistics are monotone functions of the same variance ratio; their percentile coverages coincide in these results. The integer-valued ndc has discrete steps, which can produce conservative intervals and overcoverage. The findings below identify every affected scenario and interval estimand individually.

Bias interval: coverage by scenario

This section recomputes the bias interval study using the currently loaded msa_bias() at confidence level 0.95. Item truths are the supplied references, with independent residuals for every response. The specification settings and seeds are shown below. Both scenarios use 1000 repetitions, from the minimum in ANK-06. The RNG is Mersenne-Twister/Inversion/Rejection; the caller’s random state is restored after the calculation.

scenario items prompts models reps residual item bias seed
S-bias-1 20 3 3 3 0.1 1 0.2 20261106
S-bias-2 20 3 3 3 0.5 1 0.0 20261107

Coverage counts every closed interval containing the true bias. Its MCSE is the square root of coverage times its complement divided by n_sim. Failed calculations abort with the scenario and repetition instead of dropping observations. The signed distance from the nominal level is reported in MCSE; undercoverage or overcoverage beyond the anchored reporting threshold is named in the table. The reporting threshold is 3 MCSE and the acceptance threshold is 4 MCSE (ANK-TOL.mc_factor). Reporting a finding does not change the interval or stop the table from rendering.

scenario coverage MCSE n_sim distance to level (MCSE) finding
S-bias-1 0.959000 0.006270 1000 1.435295 within report threshold
S-bias-2 0.952000 0.006760 1000 0.295863 within report threshold

Elapsed time: 7.748 seconds, with R 4.6.2 and llmsa 0.2.0. The independent class A acceptance study checks the same scenarios and each interval against the t formula. These results assess the bias interval with independent residuals; they do not establish linearity-band coverage for correlated item replicates. The installed validation/agreement/README.md records ADEMP and commands for public and repository contexts.

Robustness screening: Plackett-Burman and Lenth

The harness validates pb_design() against the published generator rows in ANK-80 and FrF2::pb(boxtyssedal = FALSE), allowing row and column permutations and column sign changes. ANK-81 supplies Lenth’s published examples and method constants. The protected example tables are checked locally against their anchored hashes. Main effects are compared with differences of level means and regression coefficients; PSE is checked against unrepx::PSE(method = "Lenth"), and PSE, ME and SME against DoE.base::ME.Lenth(simulated = FALSE). These are live oracle calculations in the acceptance suite under tests/acceptance/, with tolerances from ANK-TOL.arithmetic and ANK-TOL.frf2_unrepx. ANK-82 specifies Daniel’s half-normal plotting positions, which are checked in the recorded plot.

The class A study tests/simulation/test-lenth-h0.R uses seeded normal noise under the null hypothesis of zero effects. It checks every ME and SME decision against an independent Lenth calculation and reports the per-effect and per-experiment false alarm rates, their Monte Carlo standard errors and their distance from the nominal alpha. The sample size comes from ANK-06 and the allowance from ANK-TOL.mc_factor. The method is conservative: rates below nominal do not justify recalibrating the margins, and no factor exceeding ME does not establish pipeline robustness. This study runs in the harness; building this vignette does not rerun it.

With transform = "logit", msa_robustness() analyses finite proportions strictly between zero and one on the logit scale, including the response mean and standard deviation. Boundary proportions require a prior correction; finite empirical logits can be supplied with transform = "none". The default analyses the supplied response without transformation. Unit tests check the transformation against regression, input errors, invariance to relabelling and row order, and reproducibility of the randomised design.

System suitability and simulator validation

ANK-86 records the Westgard definitions, their strict boundaries, complete windows and standardization. The harness checks constructed boundary series and an independent rule evaluator in tests/acceptance/test-m3c-1-westgard-rules.R and test-m3c-2-r4s-reading.R. The warning rule does not reject a run. Both R_4s readings use consecutive controls; the Westgard reading requires that the compared controls belong to the same run. The interface has no run identifiers, so the caller supplies that grouping. Printed and rendered reports identify the reading and the actual positions that fired.

The class A study tests/simulation/test-westgard-false-alarm.R compares each rule’s firing rate at each position with the analytic probability in ANK-86, with Monte Carlo standard errors and the allowance from ANK-TOL.mc_factor. It separately reproduces Parvin’s ongoing procedure from ANK-87, including the in-control history before a shift, and compares inverse average run length with the published values using that anchor’s tolerance. The inverse run-length MCSE is reported using a delta approximation. These are harness studies; building this document does not rerun them.

tests/acceptance/test-m3c-4-qcc-limits.R observes the horizontal lines actually drawn by the chart and compares them with the closed formulas and live qcc::qcc(type = "xbar.one") results under a supplied center and SD. test-m3c-5-simulator-latent.R checks the item truth and mean shifts deterministically. tests/simulation/test-simulator-recovery.R uses S-sim-1 and the S-boot-1 variance components to check recovery with msa_fit() and the distribution of item truth, with seeds, versions and MCSE. The sample size comes from ANK-06 and the comparison allowance from ANK-TOL.mc_factor.

Planning rule for prompt-variance precision

The rule from ANK-89 is CV(sigma2_hat_Y) ~ sqrt(2 / nu_Y), with prompt degrees of freedom equal to the number of prompt variants minus 1. Each candidate below uses n_sim = 1000 actual repetitions. The empirical CV is the sample SD divided by the mean of all prompt variance estimates, including zeros. A boundary estimate means exactly zero, before display rounding; its share has MCSE given by the binomial standard-error formula. Singular fits remain in every denominator. Failed fits stop the generation.

plan items prompts nu cv_rule cv_empirical boundary_share mcse_boundary n_sim
S-plan-1 20 3 2 1.0000 1.0722 0.0460 0.0066 1000
S-plan-2 20 5 4 0.7071 0.7436 0.0070 0.0026 1000
S-plan-3 40 3 2 1.0000 1.0334 0.0340 0.0057 1000
S-plan-4 40 5 4 0.7071 0.7513 0.0080 0.0028 1000

The comparison is descriptive and has no pass threshold. The simple rule describes the precision of a variance estimate based on a single mean square; residual and interaction estimation and the nonnegative REML boundary affect the empirical distribution. More items do not replace independent prompt levels. The boundary shares make visible where the unconstrained approximation does not describe the fitted distribution well.

The empirical CV exceeds the rule value for S-plan-1, S-plan-2, S-plan-3, S-plan-4.

The supplementary CV MCSE below uses the delta method over the first two empirical raw moments, including the sample-SD correction and their estimated covariance. It is an approximation requiring positive mean and variance and finite moments; an undefined value is labelled explicitly. This named method is allowed by ADR-054 pending the operator’s ACC-9 decision about the formula collection. It adds no acceptance threshold.

validation/planning/README.md records ADEMP, formulas and reproduction commands. SOURCES.json and session.txt preserve hashes, methods, versions and actual elapsed times. This reader uses the public context, verifies anchor and result hashes and recomputes summaries from stored repetitions. With REPO_ROOT, the original anchors must also match. There is no automatic simulation during knitting. The class A harness test tests/simulation/test-plan-satterthwaite.R independently repeats the seeded calls and checks that this table reports the resulting numbers. Numerical changes to planning, simulation or fitting require a fresh generation run.
